newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian inmates of PLO to step up hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian inmates of PLO to step up hunger strike.

text.p: Five Palestinian prisoners plan to step up a hunger strike to protest against their detention without charge in a PLO prison for more than eight months, a human rights group said on Tuesday.
The Bir Zeit University Human Rights Action Project said the inmates, who include three university students, have been taking only water since they began their protest on November 3.
"They have grown visibly weaker. They can't even sleep. And from Friday, they told us that they intend to stop drinking water and to refuse medical treatment," said university spokesman Nigel Parry.
Parry said no charges had been filed against any of the five detainees in Ramallah prison in the West Bank.
Palestinian security officials were not immediately available to comment.

Two of the five hunger strikers were among 10 Bir Zeit students the Palestinian High Court ordered released last August. The Palestinian Authority ignored the court ruling at the time but eight were later freed.

The hunger strikers were among hundreds of Palestinians detained in a crackdown on Islamic militants after suicide bombings in Israel last February and March. Most of the detainees held at Ramallah prison have since been released, Parry said.
